articles.body: KOCHI: S Murali gave an unusual analogy to describe the struggles his son, long jumper Sreeshankar Murali, undertook to regain full fitness after a career-threatening knee injury he sustained two years ago.âSreeshankarâs comeback was as difficult as preparing for the IIT and Civil Services simultaneously,â he told TOI.Murali is currently near Prague, where he is closely monitoring his sonâs training ahead of a busy stretch that begins with the World Athletics Continental Tour (silver level) meet in Bhubaneswar on Aug 22, followed by next monthâs Asian Games in Japan.âSreeshankarâs training now revolves around strength and conditioning, along with the prehab and rehab programme designed by coach Wayne Lombard. There is very little time to work on technique. The priority is to protect the knee on his take-off leg,â Murali said.His IIT-UPSC analogy aptly captures the magnitude of the challenge Sreeshankar faced after suffering the devastating injury just months before the 2024 Paris Olympics.Two years later, the journey came full circle when the 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last weekâs Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.âOf all the medals Sreeshankar has won, this one gives me the greatest satisfaction because of the circumstances under which he achieved it. It reflects his mental toughness and hunger,â Murali said.The conditions in Glasgow were anything but favourable.âIt was around 12 degrees Celsius with drizzle and strong winds, making the runway tricky,â Murali said. Despite the difficult conditions, Sreeshankar produced a best jump of 8.09m to finish second.The performance inevitably brought back painful memories of 2024, when the family received a grim diagnosis after Sreeshankar tore the patellar tendon in his take-off leg.âThe doctors in Mumbai had not seen an injury like this. I thought he would never be able to walk again,â Murali recalled.âThey told us it wasnât a common sports injury but the kind usually seen after a serious car accident. His knee was completely ruptured.âDetermined to find the best treatment, Murali travelled nearly 1,900 miles with his son to Dohaâs Aspetar Hospital. âThe surgeons reconstructed his knee using four screws.âThe Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process.The painstaking recovery paid rich dividends. Since returning to elite competition, Sreeshankar has consistently cleared the eight-metre mark, including a seasonâs best of 8.38m at the Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar in June.âThere is no time to bask in the Commonwealth Games glory,â Murali said, pointing to the demanding schedule ahead.Sreeshankar will now turn his attention to the Asian Games in Japan, where he hopes to upgrade the silver medal he won at the previous edition in Hangzhou.âWith everything Sreeshankar has gone through, he has every reason to believe he can stand on top of the podium at the Asian Games,â Murali concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Reality check after Commonwealth Games 2026: Indiaâs boxing renaissance to face ultimate Asian exam
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Indiaâs record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indiaâs record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. After returning from Glasgow with a historic haul of seven gold and three silver medals, Indiaâs boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.The CWG triumph underlined the countryâs growing depth, particularly in womenâs boxing. Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) struck gold, while Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg) topped the podium in the menâs competition. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, Jadumani Singh and Narender Berwal added silver medals.The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya, however, will be on an entirely different scale. Unlike the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will feature continental powerhouses such as Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Chinese Taipei, Japan and North Korea â nations that have consistently dominated the World Championships and the Olympics. Uzbek stars Mirazizbek Mirzakhalilov and Bobo-Usmon Baturov, along with Kazakhstanâs Kairat Yeraliyev and Ablaikhan Zhussupov, are expected to headline a field packed with world-class talent.India will also be without two of its Commonwealth champions. Jaismine (57kg) and Arundhati (70kg) will miss out because their weight categories do not feature in the Asian Games programme, depriving the country of two genuine medal prospects.âThe Asian Games for us is like the Olympics,â Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh said. âThe best teams in the world today are Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and India, and all three are in Asia. Add a strong Chinese contingent and you understand why it is much tougher. You canât replicate this (CWG) performance at the Asian Games. But if you win a sizeable number of medals at the Asian Games, you can be hopeful of winning medals at the Olympics too.âWomenâs head coach Santiago Nieva shared a similar assessment while insisting the team remains on the right path.âWe canât guarantee that we will win gold all the time, but we are on the right track. We know how strong the field will be at the Asian Games. The boxers are aware that they canât sit on their success,â he said.India had returned with one silver and three bronze medals from the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. The Glasgow CWG showcased the strides the boxing contingent has made. But itâll be Aichi-Nagoya that is going to reveal whether the progress is enough to challenge Asiaâs finest and signal genuine medal potential for the 2028 Olympics.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Glasgow to Ahmedabad: Gujarat receives Commonwealth Games flag as 2030 countdown begins
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: The Commonwealth Games flag was formally presented to Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel on Wednesday, marking the beginning of preparations for t.
articles.body: The Commonwealth Games flag was formally presented to Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel on Wednesday, marking the beginning of preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.After returning from Glasgow, deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi handed over the flag to Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar.Sanghavi had attended the closing ceremony of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Sunday along with Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha. During the ceremony, the Commonwealth Games flag was officially handed over to India as Ahmedabad prepares to host the next edition in 2030.According to an official release, "deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi formally presented the Commonwealth Games Flag, with full honour and dignity, to chief minister Bhupendra Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar."Para-athletes Rakesh Bhatt and Rohit Majgul, who represented Gujarat at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, were present during the ceremony. Para table tennis player Sonal Patel also attended.The release added, "The Commonwealth Games Flag will now remain in Gujarat until the 2030 Commonwealth Games. Along with advancing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Fit India' vision, it will serve as an inspiration for athletes and symbolise the commencement of preparations for the upcoming event."Speaking to reporters after arriving at Ahmedabad Airport earlier in the day, Sanghavi said the city aims to set a new standard for hosting the Commonwealth Games."These Games will be organised with grandeur and with the best possible arrangements for the athletes. They will be conducted in such a way that every athlete can deliver his best performance," the deputy CM said.Sanghavi, who also holds the sports portfolio, said the Gujarat government remains committed to taking forward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Fit India movement and anti-drug campaign."We will advance the anti-drug campaign and the Fit India Movement so that the youth of the country receive maximum opportunities in the sports sector. articles.summary: Former Bangladesh captain Shakib Al Hasan’s home attacked after joining former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s event.
articles.body:
Windows were smashed and petrol bombs hurled at former Bangladesh cricket captain ⁠Shakib Al Hasan’s residence after he joined ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s first public media interaction since her 2024 removal from power, in which she pledged to return in December.

Police said ⁠a group of people attacked Shakib’s ancestral home in Magura town, about 170km (105 miles) southwest of the capital Dhaka, on Wednesday, causing a fire on the upper floor of the residence. The property was unoccupied at the time, and no injuries were reported.

articles.body:
Police in the United Kingdom have confirmed that members of the Ugandan boxing team were unaccounted for after they participated in the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

articles.title: Parker’s positive cocaine test caused by nutritionist, doping body says
articles.summary: The 34-year-old boxer tested positive for cocaine on day of shock loss to Fabio Wardley in London in October.
articles.body:
Former world heavyweight boxing champion Joseph Parker has been cleared to return to the ring after serving a three-month drugs ban that authorities said was due to his nutritionist.

The 34-year-old New Zealander tested positive for cocaine on the day of his shock loss to Fabio Wardley in London in October.

Parker has always denied knowingly taking any banned substances and United Kingdom Anti-Doping (UKAD) said the nutritionist he employed ahead of his fight with Wardley was a “regular user of cocaine”.

“New Zealand professional boxer Joseph Parker has served a three-month ban from all World Anti-Doping Code-compliant sport following an anti-doping rule violation (ADRV) for the presence of a prohibited substance,” a UKAD statement said on Thursday.

“At the time of this announcement, Mr Parker is free to participate in sport.”

“On 6 March 2026, Mr Parker provided UKAD with evidence claiming that the adverse analytical finding was the result of his exposure to cocaine used by the nutritionist he had employed in preparation for the bout on 25 October 2025.

“The nutritionist stated that he was a regular user of cocaine and had used cocaine daily in the week leading up to the bout,” the statement added.

Parker was tested by the Voluntary Anti-Doping Association (VADA) on October 25.

On the same day, he was beaten by Briton Wardley at London’s O2 Arena.

Parker failed a UKAD test in the early hours of October 26 .

UKAD added it had found in June that Parker’s cocaine ingestion had occurred out of competition and therefore was “in a context unrelated to sport performance”, thereby lifting his previous suspension.

Parker’s professional record stands at 36 wins and four defeats.

He was WBO heavyweight champion from 2016 to 2018 before losing the title to Britain’s Anthony Joshua in Cardiff.

UKAD’s statement came the day after Parker himself announced his ban had been lifted.

“I’m pleased to confirm my provisional suspension is lifted and I’ll be back in the ring soon,” he said.

Parker suffered an 11th-round stoppage defeat by Wardley and lost his status as WBO mandatory challenger to then undisputed heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk.

articles.title: World Darts Championship: 2026/27 dates confirmed for Alexandra Palace with Sunday final in Great Hall for first time
articles.summary: The 2026/27 PDC World Darts Championship is set to break records with a Sunday final at Alexandra Palace's Great Hall and a new ballot procedure introduced with 180,000 tickets on offer
articles.body:
In a major change for this year the tournament will be held in Alexandra Palace's Great Hall for the first time, which can accommodate over 5,200 spectators compared to the previous 3,200 limit.

Luke Littler went back-to-back in January when he defeated Gian van Veen in a one-sided final with the 19-year-old, who has already won the World Masters, UK Open, World Cup, World Matchplay and Premier League in 2026, ready to make it a hat-trick of wins.

For the first time in the event's history, tickets for the tournament will be allocated through a Wimbledon-style ballot, which will take place in two stages.

PDCTV annual members receive an exclusive priority window, giving them an increased opportunity to secure tickets ahead of the general ballot opening.

The PDC annual members ballot then opens at 12pm on Tuesday September 1 until Monday September 7.

The general ballot opens at 12pm on Tuesday September 8 and closes at 11.59pm on Monday September 14.

The first round will be starting four days earlier than in 2025 with 128 players involved - live on Sky Sports .

There will also be the usual Christmas break between December 24-27 with the tournament concluding after New Year's Eve.

Alexandra Palace has hosted the World Darts Championship since 2007.

articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Harsh Singh's right knee still swells. It still hurts. Every time the Indian judoka steps onto the mat, he is reminded of the ACL and menis.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Harsh Singh's right knee still swells. It still hurts. Every time the Indian judoka steps onto the mat, he is reminded of the ACL and meniscus tear that nearly derailed his career. But at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, pain took a back seat as the 23-year-old scripted history by becoming India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist."The pain never really goes away," Singh told TOI in an interview on Thursday. "Sometimes my knee still swells up and feels tight. During the CWG, I felt the pain and the knee occasionally got swollen. After surgery, the joint never became exactly the way it was before. There's always a little discomfort during fights. You have to ignore it and continue. The medal kept me going."The historic triumph came less than a year after Singh tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS) in Aug 2025. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition."I was in rehabilitation for almost a year. The entire coaching team at the IIS, recovery specialists and Spencer sir (Mackay, S&C expert) helped me throughout. They rebuilt my strength step by step. Because of the IIS and their entire team, I was able to come back on the mat, qualify for the CWG and represent India," he said.The comeback demanded another battle off the mat. Months away from competition saw his weight rise to nearly 72kg, forcing him to shed more than 12kg to return to his 60kg category. Gold at a ranking tournament and bronze at the senior National championships sealed his place in India's CWG squad.Despite lingering discomfort, Singh dominated in Glasgow, with only a hard-fought semifinal stretching him before he clinched the historic title."The semifinal (against the Australian Pedro Carlos) was the toughest. In the 60kg category, even a small point can decide the match. We didn't want to concede anything and stayed aggressive," he recalled.With CWG gold secured, Singh has already shifted his attention to next year's Asian Games. Training stints in Japan and South Korea are part of his preparations as he looks to bridge the gap with Asia's best."I want to improve my speed, grip and strength. Japanese and Korean players are very fast, so training there will help," he said.Born into a modest family, with his father working as a daily-wage labourer, Singh once trained without owning a judo uniform. Support from the govt's schemes and a privately funded athletes' training centre changed the course of his career."My life has changed because of this medal. More people have started noticing judo," he said. "But the best compliment came from my family. They told me, 'You have made the entire family proud.' That meant more than anything else."Having conquered injury to create CWG history, Singh's next aim is clear â turning a gritty comeback into an Asian Games podium finish.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Days after historic CWG gold, Dilip Gavit leaves without meeting Raj Thackeray after two-hour wait
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: Just days after scripting history for Indian para athletics at the Commonwealth Games, gold medallist Dilip Gavit found himself making headlines for a.
articles.body: Just days after scripting history for Indian para athletics at the Commonwealth Games, gold medallist Dilip Gavit found himself making headlines for a very different reason. The 23-year-old sprinter, who became India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medallist in the men's 100m T47 event, waited for nearly two hours to meet Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray in Nashik on Thursday before leaving without the meeting taking place.Invited, but left waitingAccording to Gavit's coach quoted by PTI, Vaijanath Kale, the para-athlete had been invited to meet Thackeray during the MNS chief's visit to Nashik. However, despite arriving at the scheduled venue, Gavit and his coach were made to wait for nearly two hours. A video from the venue showed MNS workers requesting the duo to wait longer while trying to explain that Thackeray was occupied."We were waiting for quite some time... Sir is busy. We will meet him later," Kale is heard saying in the video before they eventually left.A champion who made history in GlasgowThe incident came just days after Gavit delivered one of India's biggest moments at the Commonwealth Games. Clocking a Games-record 10.71 seconds, the Nashik sprinter won the men's 100m T47 gold medal, leading a historic Indian one-two finish alongside Mohammed Basil Morssinganakath, who claimed silver. The victory marked India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medal in para athletics 100m T47.A journey built on resilienceGavit's success carries a deeper significance given his remarkable journey. Born into an economically disadvantaged tribal family in Maharashtra, he lost his right arm in a childhood accident. His life changed when coach Vaijanath Kale took him under his wing at the age of 12, supporting his education and athletic development. After winning gold in Glasgow, Gavit emotionally dedicated the medal to Kale, crediting his coach for transforming his life.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bangladesh cricket’s Shakib, an Hasina ally, will face trial if he is safe
articles.summary: Sheikh ⁠Hasina ally Shakib Al Hasan will face Bangladesh trial if safety assured, with Cricket World Cup return eyed.
articles.body:
Bangladeshi cricket great Shakib Al ⁠Hasan, an ally of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh ⁠Hasina, says he is ready to return from a two-year exile, face trial on charges that include murder, and play a farewell series if the government guarantees his safety.

Shakib, a former politician for Hasina’s Awami League, has been living in the United States since her government was toppled in a deadly student-led uprising in August 2024.

Now 39, ⁠the player has not yet retired from international cricket and said he still hopes to play a farewell series at home and represent his country at the 2027 Cricket World Cup, a one-day international tournament.

The former Bangladeshi captain’s case highlights the wider fallout from Hasina’s ouster, which has left dozens of her allies facing criminal charges and unable to return to Bangladesh.

His return would test whether Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s government will accommodate figures from ⁠the former governing party — an open question as Hasina herself has announced plans to go back in December despite having been given a death sentence there.

“If I get the clearance from the government that my security will be ensured, I am happy to go back, face the court trial and everything that’s needed to be done,” Shakib told the Reuters news agency by phone from Sri Lanka, where he is playing franchise cricket.

“I know I haven’t done anything,” he said, giving the most detailed account yet of his two years abroad. Hasina, who has been living in India, was sentenced to death in absentia over the crackdown on the Bangladesh protests that killed about 1,400 ‌people, according to the United Nations.

She has told Reuters that she and other Awami League leaders plan to return to Bangladesh voluntarily in December. Shakib said he wanted to go home immediately, but failing that would try to return alongside her.

“Whatever the captain says, we follow her,” he said. “I think they will decide it better, and we will follow the instructions given to us.” Shakib defended his virtual appearance at a Delhi news conference on Wednesday alongside Hasina, after which his unoccupied house in Bangladesh was attacked, saying he had called only for peace and Bangladesh’s progress and had no regrets.

He said he had written, through a lawyer, to the Bangladeshi interior, law and sports ministries under the previous interim government as well as to the police, seeking to have what he described as fabricated charges against him dropped, but had received no response. Shakib said he was keen to talk to Prime Minister Rahman about returning.

Turning to cricket, ⁠Shakib said he would not wait long to retire.

“I am playing most of the franchise leagues. I am feeling good, still enjoying the game, playing ⁠well also,” he said. “But … age is not on my side at this moment, so I cannot wait for too long.”

On one occasion in late 2024, Shakib said, he boarded a flight home on assurances from the interim government that he would be given security. He called officials from the airport lounge to confirm he was travelling, then was told mid-journey to turn back. He landed in Dubai and returned to New York, where he lives on Long Island with his wife ⁠and three children.

“I don’t know what changed in 12 hours,” he said, adding that the trip had been arranged over the previous five to seven days.

A later return plan collapsed after he posted a birthday message for Hasina on social media, which he said authorities cited as the reason for barring his re-entry. “I don’t understand how ⁠that is the criteria for not letting me into Bangladesh,” he said.

Shakib rejected suggestions made by previous officials that distancing himself from ⁠Hasina and the Awami League could ease his return. “There is no way I will consider that.”

In 2024, the then-interim government’s sports adviser, Asif Mahmud, said Shakib would be given security like any other cricketer, but he urged the player to clarify his political stance to reduce public anger over his Awami League ties.

He said two cases against him are currently active: one over the alleged killing of a protester during the uprising, and one brought by anticorruption authorities about alleged corruption. The murder case, he said, was filed ‌on a day in August 2024 when he was playing a match in Toronto.

“It’s a laughable case,” he said, adding that he has not yet appointed a defence lawyer.

His bank accounts have also been frozen for a year and a half pending investigation, he said, though he declined to name the banks or say how much money was being withheld.

“When someone is the highest-taxed player for the last 10 years and ‌paid all ‌the taxes and everything and his account has been frozen for a year and a half for investigation,” he said. “I will give you all the information you need, but if you don’t find anything, just release it.”

Shakib said that for two years he had not seen his parents, who have remained in Bangladesh but have not been allowed to leave.

“It’s been difficult for all of us, but we are surviving.”

On Thursday, Shakib said his house had been attacked after he joined Hasina’s first public media conference since her 2024 removal from power.

articles.title: Raymond van Barneveld fined and suspended over inappropriate behaviour and offensive language in latest Darts Regulation Authority case list
articles.summary: Dutch darts legend Raymond van Barneveld, Cameron Menzies and Dom Taylor are among the high-profile players named in the latest Darts Regulation Authority (DRA) case list, published for the first time since 2022
articles.body:
The DRA, which is the independent body responsible for regulating the sport, particularly in events run under the umbrella of the PDC, WDF, Modus and ADC, has published an updated case list for the first time since 2022, listing all backdated hearings from January 2023 to June 2026, relating to various incidents that had occurred in both televised and non-televised competition.

Former world champions Rob Cross, Gary Anderson, Luke Humphries and Van Barneveld all feature in the case list, along with Cameron Menzies and Dom Taylor.

Van Barneveld, widely regarded as one of the sport's greatest-ever players, features in two separate incidents.

The first involves 'Inappropriate behaviour and using offensive language' at Players Championship 2 event in Wigan last year, resulting in a three-month suspension [suspended for 12 months] and £3,000 fine.

The second relates to 'failing to report damage caused to hotel room' following a Players Championship event in Germany, which resulted in a formal warning.

'Barney' is a five-time world champion having won the BDO tournament at Lakeside in 1998, 1999, 2003 and 2005 before making the move to the PDC the following year.

The doyen of Dutch darts made his mark by winning the 2007 PDC World Championship with a legendary final against Phil 'The Power' Taylor.

Sky Sports have contacted the DRA regarding Van Barneveld's fines.

Menzies' sanction for his outburst at the World Championship in December has been revealed , with the Scot handed a four-month suspension, which ended last month, and receiving a £2,500 fine after he repeatedly punched the underside of the drinks' table on stage in frustration following his defeat to Charlie Manby.

The incident drew blood on his knuckles, which he then wiped on his face before walking off the stage.

Shortly after the incident, Menzies issued a statement apologising for his actions.

"First of all, I would like to apologise for what happened," said Menzies. "I am sorry that I reacted in the manner that I did.

"It's not an excuse, but I have had a lot of things on my mind recently and I suppose it all just became too much at the end.

"It has not been an easy time for me with my uncle Gary passing away recently. I saw him four days before he died and he gave a look which told he much he thought of me. He treated me like a son.

"Had I won the game against Charlie, my second match would have been on the day of Gary's funeral and that has not been lost on me in recent days.

"Let me say again, that's no excuse for what I did on the stage. It was the wrong thing to do and I don't want it to take anything away from Charlie. He played well and deserved his win.

"This is not how I would like people to view me. Yes I can get emotional at times, but not like that and that wasn't right."

Taylor's failed drugs test at the World Championship resulted in a six-month suspension until June 18 , as well as a £1,275 fine in costs and the forfeiture of his £25,000 in prize money.

Taylor tested positive for cocaine and cannabis with the offence being his second which incurred a mandatory six-month ban under DRA rules.

"Accordingly, and taking into account all of the available evidence, the committee were satisfied that Mr Taylor's ingestion of both cocaine and cannabis occurred out of competition and was not following the commencement of the World Championship on 11th December 2025," the DRA statement read.

"Following on from this finding, the committee has determined that as this is Mr Taylor's second offence, then under these rules, he must serve a six month ban in line with 10.9 (a) and 10.9 (b) of UKAD Anti-Doping Rules 2021".

Taylor also lost his Tour Card as a result of the offence.

He had previously served a one-month ban in 2025 after failing a drugs test at the Players Championship Finals in November 2024. The ban was reduced from an initial two years after he agreed to undergo a UKAD-approved three-month substance abuse treatment programme.

Prakash Jiwa and Andy Jenkins both received hefty bans and were each made to pay costs of over £17,000 after being found guilty of match-fixing in the Modus Super Series from 2022-2023.

articles.title: How Jadumani Singh's risky weight change nearly derailed his CWG dream before winning Glasgow silver
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: When Indian pugilist Jadumani Singh Mandengbam stepped onto the podium to receive the men's 55kg silver medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Game.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When Indian pugilist Jadumani Singh Mandengbam stepped onto the podium to receive the men's 55kg silver medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, it marked the culmination of a journey that had almost ended before it had even begun.The 22-year-old Manipuri boxer was one of India's standout performers, winning four consecutive unanimous 5-0 verdicts to storm into the bantamweight final before settling for silver against Australia's Jye Dixon. His medal also formed part of India's historic boxing campaign, which yielded seven golds and three silvers, making the country the No. 1 boxing nation at the Games for the first time.Yet, behind that success lay months of uncertainty, selection hurdles and a weight-category gamble that nearly cost him a place on the flight to Scotland.Speaking exclusively to TimesofIndia.com, former world champion and Jadumani's mentor, Laishram Sarita Devi, recounted how the young boxer refused to abandon his Olympic dream even when every obstacle seemed stacked against him.A bold gamble after the 50kg category disappearedJadumani had built his reputation in the 50kg category, winning medals at World Boxing Cups before learning that the division would no longer feature in the Commonwealth Games, Asian Games or Olympic programme.Rather than remain in a non-Olympic category, he decided to move up to 55kg â a division already occupied by some of India's biggest names."He continued to consult with me. Whenever he had to make a big decision, he called up and consulted with me â like increasing his weight category," Sarita told TimesofIndia.com."After he won a World Cup medal in 50kg, he got to know that the weight category is no longer in the CWG, Asian Games and Olympics. He wanted to move to 55kg."The decision immediately brought fresh challenges."Army had their No. 1 boxer in the 55kg category in Pune, who is Services' No. 1 boxer. And the weight category also has Amit Panghal â Olympian and Asian champion. He said he wanted to move up the weight to compete at CWG, Asian Games etc, but was discouraged by hearing questions like whether he would be able to compete at that level, which created a doubt in him," she said.Sarita, however, wanted only one answer: "We sat down and I asked him, 'Are you confident about the decision?' He said he was, so I told him to move up the category."The selection maze before GlasgowThe decision created another problem.Without competing in the National Championships, Jadumani could not enter the national coaching camp. But because he belonged to the Army Sports Institute, Services already had its designated 55kg representative. Attempts to let him represent Manipur also failed."We tried to make him compete for the state of Manipur, but we didn't get an NOC because he is with the Army," Sarita said.Relief finally arrived through a Boxing Federation of India (BFI) policy that granted direct entries to the National Championships for World Boxing Cup medallists. The move was aimed at rewarding elite international performers and ensuring they were not blocked by the usual domestic qualification pathways.The decision allowed Jadumani to compete directly in the 55kg draw despite the institutional overlap, resulting in multiple squad members â Pawan Bartwal, Jadumani Singh and Amit Panghal â finding themselves in the same weight-category draw.Sarita said her ward grabbed the opportunity with both hands."He then got a chance to compete in 55kg in the Nationals. Due to his effort, he won against the Services No.1, Olympians etc to be named Best Boxer in the Nationals. After that he got the chance to be part of the India camp," she said.He then cleared the final selection trials, which included physical assessments alongside ring performances."He participated in the final trial for the CWG and Asian Games â which had many aspects like strength and endurance tests before fighting in the ring. He won all of it to get selected for the CWG and was really happy and started training hard," she added.The Sports Ministry hurdleJust when Glasgow appeared certain, another setback emerged.Because Jadumani had only recently moved into 55kg, he did not possess the Asian ranking required under the Sports Ministry's eligibility criteria for Commonwealth Games selection."He got an explanation mail from the Sports Ministry, which put him in immense tension ahead of the Games," Sarita recalled.Under the ministry's guidelines, boxers were expected to be ranked among Asia's top eight in their respective categories."He was ranked No. 2 in 50kg, but he lacked a ranking in the new 55kg category. He had only competed in one Asian Championship in the new weight category before the trials for CWG and, being new to the category, lost in the quarterfinals," she said.That led to fresh doubts over his selection."He was disheartened when questions were raised whether he was a medal prospect because he was not in the rankings prescribed by the ministry. He called me and said the coaches were saying he may or may not be on the flight to the CWG because of this letter from the ministry," she recalled.The uncertainty only ended after BFI submitted a detailed explanation to the ministry, outlining Jadumani's circumstances following his weight-category switch."BFI replied to the ministry properly, explaining everything and after a lot of effort his ticket to Glasgow was approved. What I like about him is that he is the kind of person who doesn't give up and has a very strong will power," she said.Why the gold slipped awayJadumani eventually reached the final after four demanding contests, each won by an identical 5-0 margin. But Sarita believes the scheduling ultimately worked against him."Jadumani's four bouts were very tough. He played all out in all the bouts till the semifinals as he got proper rest and recovery time. Since the gold medal opponent got a bye earlier, he had fewer bouts than Jadumani," she explained.The semifinal-final turnaround, she felt, proved decisive. There was a one-day gap after every bout until the semifinals, but there was no gap between the semifinal and final in Glasgow."Jadumani fought his semifinal in the evening and got the final bout the next morning only, so he did not get much time for recovery. If it was in the evening, he could have fought better. When he entered the ring for the final, I saw his face and body language sitting here and realised he had not had enough recovery," she said.The experience, she believes, underlines the growing importance of sports science."In such situations, we should look for how we can enhance or speed up the recovery process through sports science. We should discuss it to make sure our boxers can give 100 per cent every time they enter the ring," she added.Olympic gold remains the ultimate dreamSarita first noticed Jadumani as a youngster competing in a local tournament."When I saw Jadumani for the first time, it was a tournament for young boys. His movement was really pleasing and I thought he could become a good boxer in the future. I identified him at that time only and gave him Rs 500 because I was very pleased with his performance," she recalled."Jadumani did not start with me from the grassroots. He learnt his basics from another academy. He came to my academy when he was preparing to enrol in the Army Sports Institute in Pune. At that time, I did not have any infrastructure and was coaching from a makeshift setup. And then Covid happened, we had to train in a very isolated small makeshift place,â she added.Years later, after training together through difficult Covid-19 conditions and watching him overcome one hurdle after another, Sarita believes Glasgow is only the beginning."We missed gold at the CWG, but we will work hard to get gold at the Asian Games for sure," she said.The bigger ambition, however, stretches far beyond continental success."His first and primary target remains Olympic gold. Commonwealth Games and Asian Games are the stepping stones in that journey. He will try to win India's first Olympic gold medal in boxing," Sarita concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From hospital bed to CWG gold: How Jaismine Lamboria fought the odds in Glasgow
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Just weeks before stepping into the ring at the Commonwealth Games, Jaismine Lamboria wasnât thinking about medals. She was searching for a.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Just weeks before stepping into the ring at the Commonwealth Games, Jaismine Lamboria wasnât thinking about medals. She was searching for answers. The recurring fever had refused to go away.Multiple medical tests showed nothing unusual and the Indian boxer tried to push through, managing the symptoms with paracetamol. When the illness persisted, she was admitted to a hospital in Mohali. Doctors finally diagnosed a bacterial infection, putting her on an intensive 14-day course of medication. For an athlete preparing for one of the biggest competitions of the year, it could easily have been the end of the campaign.Instead, it became the beginning of one of the most remarkable comebacks of her career. âI was avoiding further medical tests because the initial reports were coming back normal. We didnât know what exactly had to be treated. Finally, after I was admitted, they detected a bacterial infection and I was on medication for 14 days,â the 57kg boxer said.When she was discharged, the clock was already ticking. Barely three weeks remained before the Games. âI started training only on July 1. Initially it was just warm-up, walking and stretching. I had very little time, so we had to be patient.âThe physical recovery was only one part of the challenge. During those uncertain weeks, sports psychologist Priya Vrinda became a constant source of support, ensuring the illness didnât break her confidence.âWhen I was sick, I was already connected with Priya Vrinda maâam. She kept me mentally strong and never allowed me to go down,â Jaismine said. That resilience was evident when she returned to competition. Jaismine boxed with maturity, tactical discipline and composure to upgrade the Commonwealth bronze she had won four years ago into gold in the 57kg.One of Jaismineâs biggest assets inside the ring has been her reach in her category. While every opponent may not be shorter â Jaismine stands five feet seven inches in her socks â she believes her physical advantage has become an important weapon thanks to careful coaching. âMy coaches taught me how to use my reach properly. articles.title: Bangladesh say Shakib will not play cricket again after Hasina event
articles.summary: Shakib Al Hasan says he will return home to face trial if safety assured, but Bangladesh rule out cricket comeback.
articles.body:
Bangladesh have said former star cricketer Shakib Al Hasan had no prospect of returning to play after he joined a media event with ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, a convicted fugitive.

Shakib joined the event by telephone in New Delhi on Wednesday, where Hasina addressed journalists, two years after she was forced from power following a deadly crackdown on student-led protests.

Bangladesh Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque said the government had previously taken a more open approach towards Shakib, who was a politician for Hasina’s former ruling Awami League party.

Shakib, who is currently in Sri Lanka, was among dozens facing murder investigations for a deadly police crackdown on protesters that toppled Hasina’s government.

“We had been looking at the matter with considerable flexibility and tolerance. After this, I do not think there is any room to think that way anymore,” Haque said in a statement.

“Someone who has taken the stage with the autocrat no longer has any opportunity to return.”

Shakib, 39, is Bangladesh’s most successful cricketer and one of the country’s best-known sporting figures. He has played more than 400 international matches and represented Bangladesh at five World Cups.

Rights groups have long accused Hasina’s former administration of abuses including the murder of rivals, suppression of opposition parties, rigged courts and one-sided elections.

A court in Dhaka found Hasina guilty in absentia in November 2025 of crimes against humanity and sentenced her to be hanged. She remains in hiding in India.

All-rounder Shakib announced his retirement plans in September 2024 after his team’s second Test in India but later said he would play a full series before calling it quits.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board said in January he could play again, but his involvement in the event in India on Wednesday caused anger, with Shakib saying his house had been petrol-bombed as a result.

On Thursday, Shakib said he was prepared to return to Bangladesh from his exile in Sri Lanka to face trial on charges including murder. He also said he hoped to play for his country again at the 2027 Cricket World Cup, having led the team at the last edition in 2023.

Ireland lost seven wickets for 63 runs on Friday as they were bowled out for 207 chasing a target of 300 at Bready Cricket Club in the Northern Irish village of Magheramason.

articles.title: British MotoGP: Raul Fernandez dominates at Silverstone to beat Martin
articles.summary: Aprilia rider’s victory over Jorge Martin extends Silverstone’s run of different Grand Prix winners to twelve in a row.
articles.body:
Trackhouse Aprilia Racing’s Raul Fernandez led from the opening lap to win the British MotoGP at Silverstone on Sunday, capitalising on an early setback for championship leader Jorge Martin.

Fernandez swept past pole-sitter Martin into turn one and never looked back, stretching his advantage to more than four seconds before taking the chequered flag 2.54 seconds clear. The victory was the Spaniard’s second in MotoGP and his first since last year’s Australian Grand Prix, completing an impressive recovery from a crash in Saturday’s sprint.

“I am really happy for the team. Yesterday (Saturday) I was quite frustrated after my mistake. But we are human and it is part of the sport,” Fernandez said.

Spain’s Martin, who won the sprint, was hampered at the start when his ride-height device failed to disengage at turn one, dropping him behind Marc Marquez and fellow Aprilia rider Marco Bezzecchi. The championship leader recovered to reclaim second from Bezzecchi on lap nine but was unable to get close enough to challenge Fernandez.

Martin’s runner-up finish extended his championship lead to 31 points, with Bezzecchi, who finished third, moving up to second in the standings. Ogura lost ground after his first retirement of the season, falling 37 points behind Martin.

“The results here are a big boost of confidence for me and the team,” Martin said.

“It seems like we found a bit of direction to get the momentum on our side now. The race was fantastic. I made a small mistake at the start, but I am glad I was able to fight back.”

Defending world champion Marc Marquez endured another difficult afternoon, finishing seventh after starting sixth on the grid and dropping to fourth in the standings.

Bezzecchi faced stiff competition from Gresini Racing’s Alex Marquez, who made a late mistake and dropped back. Alex Marquez continued to put pressure on Bezzecchi, but was unable to chase him down as the Aprilia rider finished third to secure his second podium of the weekend.

The result was particularly significant for Bezzecchi, who led the MotoGP championship earlier this season and was recording his first Sunday finish since winning his home Italian Grand Prix at the end of May.

Alex Marquez came fourth, KTM’s Pedro Acosta fifth and VR46 Racing’s Fabio Di Giannantonio sixth.

articles.title: âThat video was not ordinaryâ: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.âKya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)â Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.âWe had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,â she explained.âThat video was not ordinaryâModi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.âTo be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,â he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics.Mirabai opens up about four difficult yearsModi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.âItne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),â Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.âI was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.âThere were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,â she said.Narender's joke leaves Modi laughingThe meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.âDuring the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),â he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.âI have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.âFar more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,â Modi said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Don Nelson, Hall of Fame basketball coach and NBA player, dies at 86
articles.summary: Nelson was a five-time NBA champion with the Boston Celtics but is best remembered for his innovative coaching style.
articles.body:
Hall of Famer Don Nelson, the coach with the second-most wins in NBA ‌history, died on Sunday. He was 86.

Nelson’s family announced the passing of the five-time champion as a player but didn’t divulge the manner ⁠of death.

“On Sunday morning our ⁠beloved husband, dad, grandfather and great-grandfather Don Nelson peacefully went to be with the Lord, surrounded by his loving family,” the Nelson family statement read. “Throughout his last week, friends and family encircled him with love, sharing the blessing of his ⁠friendship and revisiting treasured memories.”

Nelson was the all-time leader with 1,335 regular-season coaching victories when he retired in 2010, and was only later surpassed by San Antonio Spurs coach Gregg Popovich (1,390). His fast style and use of smaller athletic players became known as “Nellie Ball”.

The three-time Coach of the Year didn’t win ⁠any NBA titles during his 31-year overall tenure with the Milwaukee Bucks (1976-87), Golden State Warriors (1988-95, 2006-10), New York Knicks (1995-96) and Dallas Mavericks (1997-2005). But he put together 13 seasons of 50 or more wins, twice reaching 60 (once with the Bucks and once with the Mavericks).

“[Nelson] was a true basketball visionary who saw the game differently and was never afraid to challenge conventional thinking,” the Warriors said in a statement. “His approach helped shape the game and paved the way ‌for generations of players and coaches who followed.

“More than anything, Don Nelson will be remembered for his authenticity, larger-than-life personality, and incredible passion for basketball, and his influence on the Warriors franchise will endure for years to come.”

During Nelson’s time with the Mavericks, the club had its eye on Dirk Nowitzki, a prospect from Germany, as the 1998 NBA Draft approached. During the draft, the Milwaukee Bucks tabbed Nowitzki with the ninth overall pick and traded him to Dallas.

Nowitzki developed into a big-time star during his seven seasons under Nelson. He later led the Mavericks to the 2011 NBA title, won an MVP award and was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame ⁠in 2023.

“Nellie… You believed in me,” Nowitzki said on social media. “You saw things in my game before I ⁠ever realized I could do them. I’ve said it a million times and I will always say it: I don’t think my career could have turned out how it did without you being my first coach and giving me the freedom to play my game. I can only say THANK YOU. For everything.”

Nelson was inducted into the Hall ⁠of Fame as a coach in 2012.

As a player, Nelson won five NBA titles over 11 seasons with the Boston Celtics.

He initially reached the NBA with the Chicago Zephyrs (1962-63) after being the third overall draft pick. ⁠He then spent two seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers before joining a loaded ⁠Boston team and was one of seven Boston players to average double digits in scoring in 1967-68. He averaged a career-best 15.4 points and 7.3 rebounds in 1969-70.

In 134 career playoff games, Nelson averaged 11.1 points and 4.8 rebounds. The Celtics retired his number 19 jersey in 1978.

“Don Nelson revolutionized NBA basketball through his fearlessness, ingenuity and deep conviction,” ‌NBA commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement. “He spent nearly 50 years in the NBA – winning five championships as a player with the Boston Celtics before building one of the most successful and pioneering coaching careers in league history. He brought an unmistakable personality to everything he did, and his ‌impact ‌on our sport will continue to be felt for generations.

“I send my deepest condolences to Don’s family and many friends throughout our league.”

In college, Nelson averaged 21.1 points and 10.9 rebounds in 72 games over three seasons at Iowa.

Nelson won the 2025 Chuck Daly Lifetime Achievement Award to honor his overall contributions to basketball.

articles.title: Super League's Final Charge: Leeds Rhinos, Wakefield Trinity, Wigan Warriors, Warrington Wolves, Hull KR, Leigh Leopards and St Helens in contention
articles.summary: A look at the 'Final Charge' and how the last three rounds of the Super League season are shaping up; round 25 of Super League commences from Thursday August 27, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
In Super League, the two teams who finish first and second are guaranteed a home semi-final across Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26.

In the week prior to that, the Play-Off Eliminators occur in which the third-place team takes on the team in sixth and fourth plays fifth for the chance to make it into the semis.

Then the winners of the semi-finals head to the Grand Final at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3.

Let's take a look at what each team has remaining and what is on the line for them...

Leeds Rhinos have been at the summit of Super League for a while now and they will want to hold onto that for their three remaining fixtures.

However, they are now level on points with Wigan, who briefly leapfrogged them with Friday's win over Wakefield, but they have a vastly-superior points difference after Sunday's rout of York.

They last won the League Leaders' Shield way back in 2015 and last won a trophy in 2020 when they took Challenge Cup glory, so finishing top would see a welcome return of some silverware for the Rhinos.

In their last three matches, they face St Helens (A), Wigan Warriors (A) and Hull FC (H).

After the tricky trip to face Saints, they crucially host the Warriors on September 5 so their run-in is far from an easy on, but if they can now remain unbeaten, League Leaders' Shield glory will be theirs and they will be one match from walking out at the 'Theatre of Dreams' once again.

The team who have been there, done that, and got the T-shirt. Matt Peet, head coach of Wigan, has made no secret of how hard he has been pushing for a top-two finish because he knows how crucial that home semi-final is.

Now, if his team continue on, they could usurp Leeds if they keep the pressure on with their play-off spot confirmed.

Not only that, the Warriors will be hungry to avenge their Grand Final defeat to Hull KR in 2025.

They have the Challenge Cup in their trophy cabinet and will have all eyes on adding a second piece of silverware.

Ahead of the play-offs, they still have to play Hull KR (H), Leeds Rhinos (A) and Catalans Dragons (H).

Warrington Wolves made it three wins in a jam-packed 10 days by beating Huddersfield Giants to move on to 36 points.

Their 34-24 triumph against Huddersfield on Sunday was a fifth consecutive win, putting them in the right form at the right time for the play-off charge with just three rounds to go, and they could yet even snatch top spot.

In their remaining fixtures, they face Hull FC (A), Wakefield Trinity (A) and Toulouse Olympique (H).

All of those teams are below them in the table - a luxury not afforded to many other teams in the play-off picture.

The game against Wakefield will be the toughest test, with Trinity just four points below them.

What a season it has been for Wakefield Trinity.

They are on the hunt for their highest Super League finish, but will now want to bounce back following their heart-breaking two-point defeat to top-of-the-table Leeds and then subsequent defeats to St Helens and Wigan Warriors.

In honesty, with two top teams remaining in their run-in, those results should worry Daryl Powell's side.

They have games against York Knights (H), Warrington Wolves (H) and Leigh Leopards (A) left.

Those are against two teams out of the seven still in the fight.

The team that has become renowned for coming good when they need to, Leigh Leopards want to shore up their spot in the play-offs once again.

After a disastrous start to the season, Adrian Lam's side have found their groove, made waves and look in real good nick at present.

Indeed, their win over Leeds set down a marker.

However, they have a tough end to the season in which they will know every win will matter.

The Leopards face Huddersfield Giants (A), St Helens (H) and Wakefield Trinity (H).

If Leigh want to make it to the Grand Final for the first time, they need to continue to show their steel now.

Hull KR are right in the mix and will want it to stay that way but after their loss to Warrington, they are two points off fourth spot with three games left.

The Robins were the team who did it all in 2025, ending the wait for a new team to win the competition, and now they will want to send coach Willie Peters out on a high by going back to back.

Their shock loss to Toulouse did not help their cause, though.

Their remaining matches are against Wigan Warriors (A), Huddersfield Giants (H) and St Helens (A).

St Helens have three matches to try and ensure they do not make some unwanted history.

Saints have never missed out on the play-offs. Most recently they lost 20-12 to Hull KR in the semi-finals in 2025 as the Robins went on to complete the treble.

After their loss to Hull FC, St Helens looked down and out. With triumphant wins over Wakefield and Castleford, the never-say-die attitude has been reinstated once again.

They will now refocus and aim for three wins out of three to be in with a shout. If they win all three they move to 34 points.

Not only that, they face other teams in the play-off hunt and will take on Leeds Rhinos (H), Leigh Leopards (A) and Hull KR (H).

All three their three remaining matches are against teams in the top six - talk about having to take your moment.

Will they do the unthinkable? If they do manage to win their next two, that final-round contest against Hull KR could be extra tasty...

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games News: NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as s.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off itNo state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Haryana Sports social media activityFacebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur still talking about 2023Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.Manipur Sports social media activityAnd yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. Itâs the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.Rajasthan: 14 years and countingIf there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Rajasthan Sports social media activityIts X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Uttar Pradesh and Delhi carry the same gloomy pictureGulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.UP Sports social media activityDelhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.And then come Tamil Nadu and othersSet against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.The ones somewhere in the middleNot every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.Does it matter so much?It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensationSilence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bangladesh and India battle to save cricket series after political turmoil
articles.summary: Bangladesh and India white-ball series under threat due to tensions that arose when Bangladeshi PM Hasina toppled.
articles.body:
Bangladesh is scrambling to save a six-match cricket tour against neighbouring India next month as the foreign ministers of both nations have been roped in to try to salvage the series.

Comprising three one-day internationals and three T20 matches, the white-ball series was originally planned for August last year but was postponed after diplomatic relations soured between Bangladesh and India.

“It is being worked on at the ministerial level,” Bangladesh Sports Minister Aminul Haque said late on Monday, adding that talks were ongoing between the foreign ministers.

Dhaka and New Delhi have been at odds since Bangladesh’s 2024 mass uprising toppled then-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who fled to India, her longtime ally, where she remains in hiding.

In February, Bangladesh refused to send a team to India for the T20 World Cup, citing security concerns.

The International Cricket Council refused Bangladesh’s request to play their matches in Sri Lanka, and Scotland was drafted in to replace them.

“We want to quickly resolve the deadlock that was created around the Cricket World Cup,” Haque said.

“God willing, we are hopeful that it will be resolved very soon.”

India last toured Bangladesh for a cricket series in 2022 and won a Test series 2-0. Bangladesh won the ODIs 2-1.

Bangladesh toured India in September and October 2024 for two Tests and two T20 matches. India swept both formats.

articles.title: Gian van Veen asks for help ahead of New Zealand Darts Masters with bags stuck in Paris
articles.summary: Gian van Veen arrives in Auckland for New Zealand Darts Masters - but bags stuck in Europe; Dutchman asks Qatar Airways for help as he prepares for World Series event at the weekend; Van Veen has just leapfrogged Luke Humphries as world No 2
articles.body:
Van Veen, runner-up to Luke Littler in the 2026 World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace, has already arrived in Auckland for the event - but his gear has not.

The Dutchman, who has just usurped Luke Humphries as world No 2, wrote on X, tagging Qatar Airways' support page: "I am already in Auckland, but our bags are still at Paris CDG… I will need them before this weekend's World Series tournament. Is there anyone who can help me get them here ASAP?"

Qatar Airways replied to Van Veen, apologising for the mishandled baggage and asking him to contact them directly for further assistance.

Van Veen, the winner of the European Championship in 2025 and a two-time World Youth champion, will be joined by Gerwyn Price, Stephen Bunting, James Wade, Jonny Clayton, Josh Rock, Ross Smith and Damon Heta in Auckland.

This is the fifth of six regular World Series events in 2026, with Michael van Gerwen (Bahrain Masters and Nordic Masters), Littler (Saudi Arabia Masters) and Humphries (US Masters) winning the first four between them.

The Australian Masters later this month is then followed by the World Series Finals in Amsterdam from September 17-20, an event won last year by Van Gerwen as he beat Littler 11-7 in the final.

articles.title: Rybakina defeats Osaka, advances to Canadian Open semifinals to play Gauff
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina stages a huge comeback to beat Naomi Osaka and will now play Coco Gauff for a place in the final.
articles.body:
Second-seeded Elena Rybakina fought back from a set and a break down to prevail 4-6, 7-6(5), 6-4 in her Canadian Open quarterfinal against Naomi Osaka in Toronto on Tuesday.

Rybakina, the 2022 Wimbledon and 2026 ⁠Australian Open champion, will meet fourth-seeded Coco Gauff for a place in the final after the American’s opponent, Belinda Bencic, withdrew due to a hip injury.

In ⁠the first tour-level meeting between Osaka and Rybakina, the Japanese player looked to be cruising to victory after breaking in the opening game and holding that advantage to pocket the first set.

The four-time Grand Slam champion then surged to a 4-2 lead in ‌the second set, but Rybakina rallied and came out on top in a tiebreaker to force the decider.

In the third set, the Kazakh successfully defended four break points before breaking Osaka’s serve in back-to-back games to seize control and seal victory in two hours and 33 minutes.

“This first game of the match was really tough because it cost me the set,” Rybakina said. “In the second ⁠I was just trying to stay closer to the score, ⁠even if I’m losing.

“It’s rare when you don’t play some players for so many years you’re on tour. She’s a great champion. She’s a fighter. I knew it would be a tough match.”

Earlier ⁠on Tuesday, Gauff advanced without striking a ball after Bencic withdrew from their quarterfinal, giving the American more time to ⁠fine-tune her game before the US Open.

The 2023 ⁠US Open champion is into the 16th WTA 1000 semifinal of her career as the 22-year-old chases her first title of the year.

Gauff finished runner-up in Miami and Rome before her Wimbledon campaign ended ‌in a tight semifinal defeat. She has introduced new tactical elements to her game and has looked strong in Toronto, where she has not dropped a set.

The only ‌previous ‌meeting between Gauff and Rybakina was also in Toronto, where the American won in three sets in 2022.

articles.title: Josh Kushner, Bob Iger, buying Los Angeles Lakers for record $12.5bn
articles.summary: Billionaire Mark Walter’s sale of the NBA’s Lakers is a record-breaking valuation for a North American sports franchise.
articles.body:
Venture capitalist Josh Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger are set to buy the Los Angeles Lakers, with the ⁠deal valued at a record $12.5bn, according to sources familiar with the matter, on Wednesday.

Billionaire Mark Walter purchased a majority stake in the NBA team last year in a deal that valued the club at $10bn, with the deal only having been approved by the board of governors in October.

Walter’s ⁠financial empire faces a federal probe, according to reports last month, examining links between investments held by his insurers and affiliates. Walter is also the owner of Major League Baseball’s Los Angeles Dodgers.

“As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honored for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers, one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world,” Iger and Kushner said in a statement.

“We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of [former Lakers owners] Jerry ‌and Jeanie Buss. Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans, and the city of Los Angeles.”

The two businessmen had previously been tied to a potential NBA expansion team in Las Vegas, but Wednesday’s news, which stunned fans and industry experts, seemingly ended that effort.

The deal requires sign-off from the board of governors. It is also pending due diligence by Kushner’s Thrive Eternal, a new investment strategy launched by his venture capital firm Thrive Capital, a source said.

“I want to congratulate my good friend Bob Iger and Josh Kushner on their purchase of the Los Angeles Lakers!” Lakers great Earvin “Magic” Johnson posted on ⁠social media.

“Laker fans, you couldn’t have two better owners. I’ve known Bob personally for over 40 years – he ⁠has always loved the Lakers and basketball and he will bring championships back to LA.”

As CEO of Disney, Iger oversaw sports network ESPN and built relationships with the NBA while the company entered into multibillion-dollar broadcast deals for games. He retired from Disney in March.

Iger and his wife, Willow Bay, previously acquired a controlling stake in National Women’s Soccer League side Angel City FC.

On the court, the ⁠Lakers are in a period of transition after the league’s all-time leading scorer LeBron James left the team in the offseason to join the Philadelphia 76ers.

The deal comes just weeks after Kushner emerged as a central ⁠figure in a controversial private equity plan involving global football governing body FIFA.

FIFA said in July ⁠it planned to create a new commercial subsidiary, valued at about $20bn, to hold the organisation’s World Cup and other event-related businesses and sell minority stakes to outside investors.

Thrive Eternal was expected to lead a group of investors. The proposed transaction could have raised more than $4bn for FIFA, with the proceeds intended in part to fund football development programmes around the ‌world.

The proposal triggered an immediate backlash from European football officials and others who objected to private investors taking an ownership stake in the commercial operations of the world’s most popular sport and threatened to become a test of FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s leadership.

FIFA later backed away from the plan after ‌the ‌criticism, though it said it would continue consulting on the proposed structure. Kushner’s brother, Jared, is US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law. Jared Kushner was not involved in the proposed deal.

articles.title: Swiatek sinks Svitolina to set up Rybakina title clash in Toronto
articles.summary: Iga Swiatek will face Elena Rybakina for the Toronto tennis title, as Elina Svitolina and Coco Gauff exit in semifinals.
articles.body:
Iga Swiatek outlasted Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina 6-3, 1-6, 6-3 to book a Toronto title showdown with world number two Elena Rybakina.

Australian Open champion Rybakina delivered another gutsy comeback on Wednesday, beating fourth-seeded Coco Gauff 5-7, 6-2, 6-2 to reach Thursday’s final in the hard court warm-up for the US Open.
