Former world number one Swiatek, seeded seventh, is in her first final of the year, having last lifted a trophy in Seoul almost a year ago.

She improved to 5-3 against Svitolina, who had narrowed their head-to-head record with two wins over the Polish star this year.

In a match delayed more than an hour by rain, six-time major champion Swiatek raced to a 4-0 lead in the opening set.

The Ukrainian made Swiatek work to serve it out, saving a pair of set points in the final game of the first.

Energised, she raced through the second set before Swiatek rebounded in the third, breaking Svitolina to love for a 5-3 lead before holding serve to secure the win.

“Against Elina it’s always tough, so I’m happy that I won this one,” said Swiatek.

“Especially that I came back in the third set playing better. So, yeah, that’s for sure a big improvement. I’m proud of myself.”

Svitolina, who won the Canadian crown in 2017, was seeking her third 1000-level final of the season after winning at Rome and finishing runner-up in Dubai.

But she couldn’t hang on as Swiatek upped her game again in the final set.

“Mostly, I just wanted to adjust the quality,” Swiatek said. “Because tactics can’t do much if you’re just not hitting the ball right. I knew I can do it, because I did it in the first set. I’m happy that I was patient enough to do that and didn’t get disappointed or didn’t give up.”

Rybakina sees off Gauff with another rally

Rybakina, who also rallied from a set down to beat Naomi Osaka in the quarterfinals, is on the cusp of her third title of the season after her triumph in Melbourne and a trophy in Stuttgart.

Her Canadian run has her inching closer to No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in the rankings as the August 31 start of the US Open approaches.

Kazakhstan’s Rybakina polished off the victory over Gauff shortly before 1am local time, taking advantage as the American began to falter in the face of pressure on her serve.

“She served really well in the first set,” Rybakina said. “It was pretty close the first one, and then I feel like on my serve I rushed a little bit in the end.

“I knew that I need to start straight away the second set well. I’m happy that I did a couple of good returns, and then things turned around.”

While Rybakina had to battle past Osaka to reach the semis, Gauff had advanced via a walkover. But Rybakina said the hard work may have helped her.

“I guess the adrenaline and so many hours on the court helped a bit,” she said. “In the third set also, few moments I felt like I was just swinging, and some crazy return at 30-all, and it went my way.

“So, I got my opportunities, I took them.”

articles.title: Bangladesh humble Australia with worst total in contest as Hasan takes 6-55
articles.summary: Australia dismissed for lowest total against Bangladesh as Hasan Mahmud claims career-best on Day One of first Test.
articles.body:
Hasan Mahmud took a career-best 6-55 as Bangladesh bundled Australia out for 198 to take the honours on the opening day of the first Test in Darwin.

At the close on Thursday Bangladesh were 96-1, 102 runs behind Australia.

Mominul Haque was on 35 with Tanzid Hasan alongside him on 32 as the visitors made a superb start to a Test match most people expected them to lose inside three days.

Earlier, Hasan led an impressive display by the visitors’ seamers as Australia slumped to their lowest Test score against Bangladesh, their previous worst being 217 in Mirpur in 2017.

The 26-year-old was the pick of the attack, but he was ably supported by fellow quicks Taskin Ahmed and Ebadot Hossain, who took two wickets apiece.

“I was just trying to bowl line and length, trust the process and follow what the captain was saying,” Hasan said.

“(Taskin and Ebadot) were trying their best and they did very well also.”

Steve Smith was the only Australian to offer any resistance, scoring 71, while the rest of the batsmen looked out of sorts against the disciplined attack.

“We haven’t played a Test match for a while and it can take some time to get into it,” Smith said.

“It wasn’t easy. The ball was doing stuff and you have to be patient.

“Perhaps we got dragged into a few we didn’t need to, but that’s the pressure.”

After skipper Pat Cummins chose to bat on a perfect Darwin day, a full-strength Australia were expected to dominate a Bangladesh side well-beaten by a Cricket Australia XI in their only warm-up match.

Hasan made the initial breakthrough in the 12th over with the score on 45.

Jake Weatherald, on 23, had a huge swipe at a ball outside off stump and only managed a thick edge to wicketkeeper Litton Das.

Hasan struck again soon after, fellow opener Travis Head chopping on for 22 to leave Australia 52-2.

Bangladesh then saw a huge opportunity go begging when Smith, on two, edged Ebadot to third slip where Tanzid Hasan spilled the chance.

Smith had a second escape next over when he got a thick edge off Taskin only for the ball to fly through a vacant third slip.

Marnus Labuschagne, on one, wasn’t so fortunate.

He poked at an Ebadot ball outside off stump and edged to Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto at second slip, leaving Australia 61-3.

Cameron Green came in and played some big shots before chipping Taskin to short midwicket, where Mushfiqur Rahim took an easy catch.

Wicketkeeper Alex Carey looked in good touch after lunch and cruised to 19 until he played on to Ebadot with the score on 129.

Taskin then produced the ball of the day to beat Beau Webster’s bat and clip the top off stump to leave the home side struggling on 152-6.

Cummins tried to steer the hosts to tea without further loss; however, Shanto brought Hasan back into the attack with immediate success, the Australian skipper getting a big edge to Litton.

Hasan got his fourth in the same fashion, Mitchell Starc getting a thin edge to the keeper with the score on 172.

Smith threw his wicket away going for a big hit before Nathan Lyon was last man out in similar fashion.

Bangladesh started their reply confidently and eased to 36 before Australia got the breakthrough, Shadman Islam (20) getting a leading edge off Mitchell Starc to Lyon at backward point.

articles.title: Russell Westbrook announces NBA retirement after 18 seasons
articles.summary: Westbrook, a former NBA Most Valuable Player, holds the record for the most career triple-doubles in league history.
articles.body:
Triple-double king and former NBA MVP Russell Westbrook ‌announced his retirement after 18 seasons on Wednesday via social media.

“Sometimes you don’t even know when you’ve already ⁠watched the end. You ⁠had to be there. And now it’s over,” Westbrook wrote on his social media post.

list 3 of 4 Bangladesh humble Australia with worst total in contest as Hasan takes 6-55

Westbrook’s decision was announced during a three-and-a-half-minute video. He didn’t respond to any of the questions by the ⁠narrator, but the theme made it clear Westbrook was leaving on his own terms.

At the end of the video, the screen read: “The greatest thing he left behind couldn’t fit inside a museum. It never had to be said.”

Westbrook, 37, ⁠recorded 209 triple-doubles, including a record 42 during his stellar 2016-17 Most Valuable Player (MVP) season. He averaged a career-high 31.6 points to go with 10.7 rebounds and 10.4 assists that season to become the first player since the legendary Oscar Robertson (1961-62) to average a triple-double over a full season.

A nine-time All-Star, he ranks fifth all-time in career assists (10,351) and 14th in scoring (27,176). Westbrook led the NBA ‌in assists three times and scoring twice.

In 2021, Westbrook was named to the NBA’s 75th Anniversary Team. He was named All-Star Game MVP in consecutive seasons (2015, 2016) and won a gold medal with the United States in the 2012 Olympics in London.

He averaged 20.9 points, 8.0 assists and 6.9 rebounds in 1,301 regular-season games with seven franchises.

In 135 career playoff games, Westbrook averaged 22.5 points, 7.1 assists and 6.7 rebounds.

Oklahoma City and Westbrook’s run to the NBA Finals

Westbrook was selected fourth overall by the Seattle SuperSonics in the 2008 NBA Draft, and the franchise relocated to Oklahoma City before his rookie season.

Westbrook spent 11 seasons ⁠with the franchise and teamed with Kevin Durant to make the Thunder one of ⁠the top teams in the NBA. Oklahoma City reached the NBA Finals in 2012, when James Harden was also on the team, before losing to the Miami Heat.

Westbrook made eight of his All-Star appearances with the Thunder. His other was when he averaged 27.2 points for the Houston Rockets ⁠in 2019-20, his lone season with the team.

“Russell Westbrook is the ultimate competitor,” Oklahoma City general manager Sam Presti said in a statement. “His internal belief and unbridled fearlessness helped establish the ⁠foundation of our organization from day one in 2008 and he elevated ⁠the confidence and inspired our community in every year thereafter.

“Russell will be as successful in his life after basketball as he was during his career because his qualities and gifts transfer. His impact on our community is still felt today, and he is beloved for his devotion as much as his ‌talent.

“He built a Hall of Fame career not by making statements or simply by breaking records, he did it by showing us all the power of asking one simple question: Why Not?”

Westbrook bounced around to five teams over his last ‌six ‌seasons. He averaged 15.2 points and 6.7 rebounds in 64 games (with 58 starts) for the Sacramento Kings last season.

Westbrook was a college star at UCLA before leaving for the NBA after two seasons. He was the Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year as a sophomore.

articles.title: The Hundred 2026 awards: Stuart Broad, Nasser Hussain, Lydia Greenway pick best local player, overseas player, newcomer, fielder, captain and more
articles.summary: Nasser Hussain, Stuart Broad, Lydia Greenway pick their best local player, overseas player, newcomer, value for money, fielder, captain for 2026 Hundred season in men and women's competitions
articles.body:
" Jos Buttler is into the eliminator with Manchester Super Giants. Batting three, he's scored vital runs at vital times.

"He's England's best-ever white-ball batter. He's the icon of that MSG franchise.

"He's a leader in that changing room and he's got a chance of lifting the trophy."

" Ben Duckett went straight to the final with Trent Rockets and avoided the eliminator. That's how well he's played.

"Top of the order, he plays spin, plays fast bowling, hits it in unusual areas. He's been brilliant in the field.

"Also, at the top of the order, the way he's set the tone for that middle order of the Trent Rockets, it's just nice to see Duckett playing with such confidence and such flair.

I mentioned his fielding as well, which we do have a section on, but he's been excellent. I'm very impressed."

"I've gone for the leading wicket taker in the tournament, Tilly Corteen-Coleman . I think she's taken 13 wickets.

"The reason I picked her, she's just been really consistent. Not just this season but over the last couple of seasons.

"It's great to see her top of the tree with the wickets."

" Mitch Marsh has played some really eye-catching innings. He's batting at one of the best batting services in the country at Headingley, and he's been really entertaining.

"He's done exactly what you want an overseas player at the top of the order to do. He's led from the front. He's set the tone. He's guided his teams to win.

"His average is higher when they win than when they lose, which means he's playing a key role in winning games. Look at his strike rate, nearly 170.

"So I think he's been really crucial and a really clever signing."

" Mitch Marsh. Compare his consistency to someone like Harry Brook. Now, Harry's a very fine player, but a lot of his runs have come at Headingley on that belter of a surface.

"Mitch Marsh knows Headingley well, he's got Test runs there. He loves it, but he's also gone away from home at Trent Bridge, Manchester. He's got runs all around the country.

"I like the way he's a very simple person. He's a very simple player. You pitch it up, he belts it straight back past you. You drop your length back just a fraction and he'll pull you for six.

"I just love the way he keeps it very simple. And for an Aussie, he's a really nice top bloke."

"Overseas player has to be Phoebe Litchfield . She's obviously the leading run scorer, and the way she's gone out and dominated bowling attacks has been really entertaining to watch.

"She looks as if she's in the form of her life. She's the hardest player to set a field to in the competition.

"She hits straight down the ground, she hits behind square and then she can open up square of the wicket on both sides. She's got that ridiculous switch hit.

"If I was a captain against her, I would literally have no idea where to set the field to. She's absolutely the player in form at the moment."

"Mitch Marsh is new to The Hundred. This is the first year he's played in The Hundred. So if he's new and he's come here from Australia, I have him as a newcomer.

"He had never played a Hundred game before this, I'm taking his age away from it."

"I've gone for a young player who's had his first go, not in franchise cricket but in The Hundred, LD Pretorius .

"No one's really seen him in England, not really heard of him. He's not scored Ashes centuries.

"Pretorius, to me, he's playing on a difficult surface at Lord's, he's played some beautiful shots.

"He's got clear strength through the offside. A pick-up over square leg, which is fantastic.

"He's a really stylish player, and he's one of those newcomers the world of cricket will know a lot of in five years' time."

"I've gone for Charley Phillips . She has come in and really made the most of her opportunity. She's taken some big scalps as well within the seven wickets she's taken.

"And she's bowled in different phases of the game."

"I've gone Calvin Harrison , because he came in late as a replacement player.

"Around about £31,000 was the replacement figure. And he's bowled beautifully. He's got eight wickets.

"He's fielded really well, we've seen some of his extraordinary catches, but I just think to come in at the last moment and play, he's a real talented cricketer.

"That's someone England should be looking at across formats. He bats very well - he hasn't had much chance with the bat because the Trent Rockets have been so good - but value for money, I'm going Calvin Harrison and what he's done for the Trent Rockets."

"I completely agree with Nasser. Calvin Harrison's been absolutely superb and now it's my time to be honest and say I've got this completely wrong with Adil Rashid , because he's on £250k to play!

"Yes, he's been very successful but as Nasser, I think, got newcomer wrong, I might have got value for money wrong because a quarter of a million pounds is quite a lot of money for eight games.

"He's been fantastic, Adil Rashid, as he was going to be.

"He's one of those players that I think every single team would have been talking about at the start of the auction. You know what you're going to get. He just delivers time after time.

"His leg spin, which is always crucial. We're in a dry spell, so it's going to spin a little bit more.

"He's one of those players that could have gone for a lot more. When you're talking about Harry Brook at £465k, Jofra Archer at £450k at the same franchise, that's where I sneaked in my value for money, because he's virtually half the price of Archer, but he performs.

"I've gone for Charley Phillips again here. I think she was a bargain at £15k.

"It's brilliant to see a player like her in the form that she's been in.

"And the wickets that I've mentioned, she's got big wickets. She's got Sophie Devine, Georgia Voll has been in there, Phoebe Litchfield as well, Hollie Armitage.

"So she's just been able to go in, has got quite a slingy action and just hits the top of off-stump. So it's been a pleasure to watch."

" Adil Rashid. Because in an era when spin bowlers have to bowl it quickly, have to bowl it into the surface, I still love the fact that Adil Rashid is brave enough to toss the ball up with all the variations.

"He's right at the top of his game, in an era where spinners sometimes just bowl darts.

" Trent Boult . He's done a few quirky things on the field, celebrations. He particularly upset Jonny Bairstow at Lords, but that was his ball of the tournament for me, the inswinger into the bottom of leg stump.

"I spoke to Jonny and think it was a bit of choice language that sent him off, but that's what Trent does. He's a little bit unusual at times, but he's an incredible bowler.

"I'm just drawn to him. Every time he gets a new ball in his hand, something's going to happen.

"There was a wonderful anti-fist pump that I saw with Mitch Santner. He put it in, Mitch came out, he withdrew it, and it was all a bit awkward, but Trent found that really funny."

"I've gone Nat Sciver-Brunt . The fact she hasn't always played the games, obviously she has been managing that calf injury, but when she comes in she looks as if she's never been away from the game.

"I was watching her in her last game and she wheeled out a reverse sweep first ball and it just shows the class of her, not to just get a score under her belt, but to do it at a decent strike rate.

"She's a player I always enjoy watching. Strong off the back foot, can play little dink shots, but manages the situation, manages the tempo and offers a huge amount obviously for the Rockets."

"I'll fix this a little bit, because Chris Jordan, for me, is the best fielder and has been throughout The Hundred every year, but I just could not leave out this catch from Will Jacks .

"It was Pretorius at the crease, and he was batting really well, and the members were sat watching that right in front of them.

"The first bit of the catch was hard, the second bit was remarkable."

"Catches are easier than run-outs, so that's why I chose this from Ben Duckett .

"A brilliant bit of work from Duckett, diving to his left, picking the ball up, throwing it when he's turning, and most importantly, it doesn't matter if you run out Trent Boult but it does matter if you run out Nicky Pooran.

"A brilliant bit of work to hit the stumps when you only have one to aim at. I thought that really changed that game."

"I've gone for Bess Heath actually. In terms of number of catches, she isn't up there, but I love her approach.

"For any young girl, if you're at a ground and you're watching Heath, you can tell she's got that mentality of wanting the ball to come to her.

"She doesn't shy away from catches. She made one absolutely stunning catch. A lot of players would have sat back, they would have let it bounce once and would have taken the ball and it wouldn't have even been an opportunity.

"She's been a real sort of entertainer and energetic person in the field, which adds so much value to a team when you're out there."

"Sam Billings. He's won the last three Hundred titles with Oval Invincibles, he's gone to Trent Rockets, and first of all it was a brilliant signing from Trent Rockets, knowing his leadership capability.

"Once he's been given the role at a ground that he's not captained in a huge amount at before, Trent Bridge, he's got to know what the crowd like, he's got to know the surface very well.

"He leads his players brilliantly, they're top of the table, deserve to be top of the table, straight to the final, which was always the goal for the Trent Rockets, and he's got a hell of a chance to go four from four."

" Sam Billings . I like his aggression and the fact he's got a point to prove.

"He did an interview after he beat MI London - he was there for three years and unceremoniously sacked by them, let's be honest, after everything he'd done - and he's gone to his next franchise and he's proving a point.

"He loves this tournament. It's almost the latter stages of his career, it's what makes Sam Billings the cricketer he is."

"I've actually gone for Dani Gibson because if people remember the SunRisers Leeds went on a run of three losing games. They couldn't get a win for love nor money, but she and her team managed to turn it around.

"They're now finding some form at a really good time.

"For someone like Dani Gibson, it's the first time she's captain in a tournament on this sort of stage, so I've loved how she's done it.

"I love how she's spoken to the media and just the energy that she brings on the field.

"Tactically, clearly she'll always be learning. She's obviously got Adrian Birrell, who she's working closely with as a head coach. I've really enjoyed watching her this season."

articles.title: England bolters: The names putting their hand up despite not being in performance squad with Umyla Hanley, Tom Holroyd included
articles.summary: England will head to the Rugby League World Cup in Australia in October; Brian McDermott will be tasked with choosing a squad to go; 38-man performance squad was announced in June
articles.body:
Back in June, new England head coach Brian McDermott announced a 38-man performance squad, including 10 uncapped players, with whom he would work over the season to get England as well prepared as they can be for the tournament come October.

Leeds Rhinos star and reigning Man of Steel Jake Connor has not played for his country in seven years and was overlooked by then England coach Shaun Wane for the 3-0 Ashes defeat at home to Australia last autumn. But now, he is back.

The 10 newbies include Wakefield Trinity's Jake Trueman and Caleb Hamlin-Uele, Wigan Warriors' Sam Walters and Zach Eckersley, Hull KR's Dean Hadley and St Helens' Harry Robertson.

But is all hope lost for those not in those 38 names? Could some players make a late surge?

Let's take a look at who has been playing their way into potentially being a late bolter for England...

Tom Holroyd has hit incredible form in the middle-to-late stages of this season and has become the definition of super-sub.

His physicality and impact has been clear for all to see and indeed, even his head coach Brad Arthur believes he has to be considered for a place on the plane if England want a point of difference. Arthur also touted Cameron Smith for a place too.

"I think Cameron (Smith) and Tom are showing off the bench that they could provide a really good option for that team," Arthur said.

"Tom, with his impact and his aggression, and Cameron - he comes on, and he can just change the point of attack with his footwork, his pass, and his offload.

"And I just think if you're going to try and beat Australia, you're not going to be able to defend your way to victory; you're going to need to be able to score points and both of those guys can help with that."

England have a lot of options in the middle but you would not be shocked if Holroyd is on the radar now too.

Since returning from injury, Umyla Hanley has really been impressing for Leigh Leopards, especially in attack.

Indeed, he was included in the Man of Steel panels considerations for the middle part of the season then was key in Leigh's massive win over Leeds in round 23.

Similarly to Arthur with Holroyd, Leigh head coach Adrian Lam has gone into bat for his man and believes that he has a big international future ahead of him.

"That tackle that he made at the end of the game on Ryan Hall to get his foot across the line- if anyone had said to me, 'someone's going to save you a try at the end of the game' - I would have said it was him, and all of his team-mates would have said it was him," Lam said.

"He's the ultimate competitor I've coached. No, he's the number one player I've coached in my life that competes better than anyone, and I challenge that to anyone in Super League."

Speak to any Wigan fan and they will tell you how integral Oliver Partington has been in their 2026 Super League campaign.

A work horse, he does all the hard yards that make someone the ultimate team-mate and he is willing to put his hand up for anything.

They say that what matters in big games are not the sparkling moments but the effort areas and Partington excels in those every single time.

While he will have a lot of competition in his position, he is someone who has been a standout in 2026.

Yes, he is not in Super League but it would be remiss of me to overlook Matty Nicholson.

He has returned for the last couple of games off the bench for the Raiders and if he finds a run of form, he will be someone very much in McDermott's thinking.

The new England boss has said he will firmly have eyes on the NRL as well as Super League and with that in mind, Nicholson has a real chance to get back into the international scene.

England 38-man performance programme group :

Junior Nsemba, Ethan Havard, Luke Thompson, Sam Walters, Brad O'Neill, Jake Wardle, Harry Smith, Zach Eckersley (all Wigan Warriors), Kallum Watkins, Mikolaj Oledzki, Ash Handley, Jake Connor (all Leeds Rhinos), Ben Currie, Danny Walker, George Williams, Matty Ashton (all Warrington Wolves), Kai Pearce-Paul (Wests Tigers), Dean Hadley, Jez Litten, Mikey Lewis (all Hull KR), Morgan Smithies, Jayden Brailey (both Canberra Raiders), Victor Radley, Billy Smith (both Sydney Roosters), AJ Brimson (Gold Coast Titans), Jack Welsby, Alex Walmsley, Daryl Clark, Harry Robertson (all St Helens), Morgan Knowles, Herbie Farnworth (both Dolphins), Mike McMeeken, Caleb Hamlin-Uele, Jake Trueman, Tom Johnstone (all Wakefield), Matt King (Canterbury Bulldogs), Ben Talty (Brisbane Broncos), Dom Young (Newcastle Knights).

articles.title: Super League receive investment offer from Australia's National Rugby League as part of 'recapitalisation project'
articles.summary: Super League have received an investment offer from Australia Rugby League Commission (ARLC) who run the NRL; Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season - including two matches in each round exclusively live
articles.body:
Conversations have long been occurring between Australia's governing body and Europe's, with a formal offer now having been received.

In a statement, Super League said: "RL Commercial can confirm that a first offer has been received from the ARLC (Australian Rugby League Commission) as part of the sport's recapitalisation project.

"The Super League clubs have been informed this morning.

"Details of the offer remain confidential."

Former NRL chief executive Andrew Abdo spoke to Sky Sports back in April about the NRL's planned involvement in Super League. He was over in the UK for talks about the move.

He said it was a move focused on the "globalisation" of rugby league with a view to ensure that rugby league in the UK and Europe is governed by an independent commission, similar to the set up of the ARLC.

ARLC Chairman Peter V'Landys is now understood to be leading the talks.

"We really believe in the globalisation of rugby league," Abdo told Sky Sports .

"This is a great game and we want to take it to as many people as possible. We want to win as many fans as possible.

"So while the game is growing really well in the southern hemisphere, we also want the game to be strong here in the north.

"This is about a partnership where we can collaborate on how we can grow the game, how we can grow revenues and how can those revenues be pumped back into the game?

"That's pretty nuanced and that's something we have to develop together."

RL Commercial managing director Rhodri Jones added on the talks from April: "They would like to have a heavy influence on the commission and who sits on that commission.

"What they perhaps haven't understood in totality is the make up of our governance structure in this country.

"We have multiple organisations in RFL, Super League and RL Commercial. When it is such a big topic like recapitalisation, it is complex.

"But with hard work, better detail, we can overcome some of these challenges so we can get to the right result that the sport wants."

The talks have now moved into the next negotiation phase.

Former Kangaroos half-back Cherry-Evans, widely considered one of the best playmakers in the history of the sport, is no stranger to shock moves, joining Sydney Roosters from Manly Sea Eagles for 2026 after 15 years with the club.

It had been rumoured that Cherry-Evans, who played for Australia across nine years, could be retiring at the end of this season but instead, he will make the move to Super League as he turns 38.

The Black and Whites will have Steve McNamara in charge from next year and they will have an NRL stalwart pulling the strings as well.

articles.title: Super League: Leaders Leeds Rhinos suffer first home defeat of season as Leigh Leopards claim surprise 20-16 win at Headingley
articles.summary: Super League leaders Leeds suffer first home defeat of season as Leigh pull off upset; Warrington go third with win over York; Hull KR ease past Catalans; Sky Sports will show every Super League game live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live
articles.body:
Wing Senior went over twice in the first half after team-mate Josh Charnley's effort had cancelled out Ryan Hall's opener for Leeds, for whom Brodie Croft also touched down before the break.

In balmy, energy-sapping conditions after the hottest day in the UK this year, Leigh scored a fourth try through centre Umyla Hanley early in the second period and then withstood heavy pressure to seal a deserved win.

Ryan Hall thought his late effort for Leeds had tied the scores, but his foot was clearly in touch as he grounded the ball in the corner and Leigh clung on.

Hall touched down in the corner for the opening try in the second minute after taking Jake Connor's quick pass following a high kick, but Leigh's response was immediate as Charnley raced over following Hanley's line break.

Connor's penalty in front of the posts for a shoulder barge on Kallum Watkins edged Leeds 8-6 ahead, but Leigh piled on the pressure midway through the first half and got their reward.

Senior powered over near the touchline and despite Leeds full-back Lachlan Miller's brilliant tackle, the video referee ruled the Leigh winger had dotted down before going out of bounds to put his side 10-8 up.

Leeds came roaring back when Croft burst through a gap under the posts for a converted score to nudge them 14-10 in front.

Rhinos centre Jack Bird went off for a head injury assessment following a clattering tackle and was replaced by teenager Zak Lloyd, whose terrific last-ditch tackle halted Charnley soon after.

But quick hands saw Leigh spin the ball left for Senior to go over on the outside to level the scores at 14-14 at half-time after Cook had missed his second conversion attempt.

Connor landed his second penalty to give Leeds a two-point advantage soon after the restart following Cook's off-the-ball block on Ash Handley.

Leigh responded again though, carving open the Rhinos' defence via another slick handling move that sent Hanley over for the visitors' fourth try of the match, with Cook adding the extras to put them 20-16 in front.

The visitors were reduced to 12 men when second row Andy Badrock was sin-binned for his dangerous tackle on Harry Newman with 17 minutes to go.

Leeds threatened to make their extra man count, but they lacked composure and failed to execute in the face of some desperate, scrambling defending from Leigh.

With three minutes remaining, Leeds thought they had drawn level when Handley sent Hall over in the corner following Connor's high kick.

But the video referee revealed the winger's foot was in touch as he grounded the ball and Leigh held firm before celebrating an impressive win.

Leeds' defeat gives Wigan Warriors the chance to move level with them at the top of the table on 36 points when they visit struggling Bradford Bulls on Sunday.

The victory kept Leigh on course for the playoffs as they tightened their grip on sixth by moving six points clear of St Helens, who can claim a maximum of 10 points from their five remaining games.

Warrington Wolves beat York Knights 30-10 at the Halliwell Jones Stadium to move back up to third.

York had taken an early lead after Warrington failed to deal with a high kick and Paul McShane went over in the corner.

The Wolves - looking to edge ahead above play-off rivals Wakefield - then got themselves in front after nine minutes when Josh Thewlis darted through to slide in under the posts and Ewan Irwin added the extras.

The Knights, though, soon responded again when Cody Hunter's low kick was not gathered by the Warrington backline and Jon Bennison latched onto the loose ball in the right corner.

Sam Stone, returning to the side following a three-month injury lay-off, chased George Williams' kick on the left wing and dived full length to just touch the ball down as he slid off into the advertising boards, before 18-year-old Irwin scored a fine individual try, stepping inside to burst clear, and his penalty then put Warrington 18-10 ahead at half-time.

York were punished for giving away penalties early in the second half when hooker Danny Walker took the ball a couple of yards out to spin under the posts.

Irwin then picked up a loose ball to sprint clear and run in a 60-yard try - but his celebrations were cut short after a lengthy video review decided James Bentley had knocked Denive Balmforth's arm, which caused him to fumble possession.

After a breakaway from Hunter, which looked set for a York try, was called back for what looked a tight offside call, Warrington made sure when Aaron Lindop went over in the corner after Albert Hopoate had tapped back a high kick and Irwin then slotted over a late penalty.

Hull KR maintained their push for a home play-off with a comfortable 28-10 victory over Catalans Dragons .

The home side led 22-6 after a dominant first half that saw Jack Broadbent touch down twice as Jez Litten and Joe Burgess also scored.

Tyrone May all but sealed victory with the first score of the second half after 62 minutes, before Tommy Makinson hit back with a late consolation try for Catalans.

The victory kept Hull ahead of Leigh in fifth on points difference, and moved them within just two points of Warrington and Wakefield in third and fourth.

articles.title: Prichard Colon dies from boxing injury that resulted in 221-day coma
articles.summary: Prichard Colon suffered neurological damage that required emergency surgery following a boxing bout in 2015.
articles.body:
Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33, 11 years after sustaining life-changing brain injuries in the ring.

The Puerto Rican was one of the sport’s rising stars when he was left comatose for 221 days following a fight with United States boxer Terrel Williams in 2015.

The super-welterweight bout in October 2015 was awarded to Williams in the ninth round on disqualification after Colon’s team removed his gloves, with the fighter complaining of dizziness.

Colon alleged during the fight that Williams had repeatedly struck him on the back of the head, an illegal punch in boxing known as “rabbit punches”.

The referee for the bout awarded Colon one point as punishment to Williams after a complaint about one of the punches.

Colon collapsed on return to his dressing room and was diagnosed with a subdural haematoma, and he underwent emergency brain surgery, after which he was comatose.

After awakening from the coma, the extent of Colon’s neurological damage was fully understood and he required round-the-clock care for the rest of his life.

His father, Richard Colon, announced his son’s passing late on Thursday on Facebook: “I regret to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world. Now he is in a better world.”

Colon, who was at home with his family in Florida when he died, had an unbeaten boxing career of 16 fights, with 13 wins by knockout, prior to meeting with Williams.

The bout in Fairfax, Virginia, US, has long haunted the sport with questions regarding its safety .

Williams, who himself was a star of the sport at the time with a 15-0 fight card and 12 by knockout, fought again in 2017 and 2019, but said the events following the meeting with Colon affected his life and career.

“My heart dropped, my stomach dropped. I’m praying for him multiple times daily to make a full recovery. I cannot enjoy this victory. I’m worried about Prichard,” Williams, who was 31 at the time, said shortly after the fight in an interview with The Los Angeles Times.

articles.title: Tanzid makes history as Bangladesh dominate first Australia Test
articles.summary: Tanzid Hasan hits first Bangladesh ton in Australia as tourists close Day Two of first Test on 351-6, leading by 153.
articles.body:
Tanzid Hasan became the first Bangladeshi to score a Test century in Australia as the visitors dominated to reach 351-6 at stumps on the second day of the first Test in Darwin.

Inspired by a superb 101 by opener Tanzid and an entertaining 84 from captain Najmul Hossain Shanto on Friday, Bangladesh lead the hosts by 153 runs with four wickets in hand.

Mehidy Hasan Miraz was not-out 32 at the close after being dropped by Cameron Green on the last ball of the day, with Hasan Mahmud alongside him on 13 after a gritty 40-run partnership.

“They batted really well obviously,” Australian opener Jake Weatherald said.

“We missed a few chances but all credit to them.

“The wicket’s changed a bit since our first innings so we’re excited to get out there – it looks like a really good batting track.”

Tanzid batted brilliantly in perfect conditions in the Northern Territory capital as Bangladesh chase a maiden Test win in Australia at the third attempt.

Playing just his second Test, the 25-year-old looked in complete control against the Australian attack to make a piece of history.

He had a let-off on 62 when he edged Nathan Lyon to first slip, where the usually reliable Steve Smith couldn’t hold on to a sharp chance.

Tanzid brought up his ton with a push through mid-off off Lyon midway through the second session.

He took 188 balls to reach triple figures, hitting eight fours and a huge six off Lyon.

He perished soon after, trying to hit Lyon out of the ground but only finding Mitchell Starc at deep mid-off.

Bangladesh were hoping for a good start to the morning after a superb opening day when they bowled the much-vaunted Australians out for 198.

Tanzid and Mominul Haque did just that, starting the day at 96-1 and batting comfortably through the first hour’s play.

The Australian bowlers were much improved on Thursday’s efforts, but the Bangladesh pair played patiently, taking singles when on offer and waiting to pounce on the rare bad balls.

Tanzid brought up his half-century shortly before the first drinks break of the day, reaching his 50 off 102 balls.

Mominul looked certain to join Tanzid in reaching the milestone, but on 49 he tried to punch a Josh Hazlewood ball through the offside, only managing a thick edge to wicketkeeper Alex Carey.

The pair put on 102 runs and took Bangladesh to 138-2, 60 runs behind the Australian first innings.

Skipper Najmul joined Tanzid at the crease and immediately increased the scoring rate against a tiring Australian attack.

That accelerated further when Mushfiqur Rahim joined his captain following Tanzid’s dismissal.

They looked like putting the match beyond Australia’s reach with some attacking stroke play.

But the second new ball came to Australia’s aid as the Bangladeshis lost Najmul, Mushfiqur (36) and Litton Das (0) in quick succession, all caught at second slip by Smith.

The three catches took Smith to equal Joe Root as the most catches by a fielder in Tests.

The Australians must have thought they would wrap up the Bangladesh innings and be starting their second innings by the end of the day, but Mehidy and Hasan dug in and slowly took the lead past 150.

articles.title: Swiatek defeats Rybakina to claim Canadian Open title​
articles.summary: Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek defeats Elena Rybakina in Toronto to claim the WTA Canadian Open title.
articles.body:
Iga Swiatek captured her first title of the ⁠season with a swift ⁠6-2 6-3 win against Elena Rybakina in the Canadian Open final, giving the Pole a confidence boost heading into the US Open.

It was Swiatek’s first final at ⁠the US Open tune-up event, and the six-times Grand Slam champion enjoyed the Toronto crowd chanting “Iga! Iga!” throughout the match on Thursday on her way to victory, with a few Polish flags in the crowd.

But Swiatek ⁠told Canadian network Sportsnet that she felt angry after the win, having faced criticism from media back home amid an inconsistent season that has seen her fail to advance beyond the quarterfinals at a Grand Slam and replace her coach.

“I think that’s the first time in my life I have something like that after a ‌victory but it hasn’t been easy you know,” said Swiatek. “I’m happy that I kept my composure, kept my focus, and I keep growing every month no matter what the challenges and I’m super proud I could win this one.”

The Pole was sharp and fast on the hard court in Toronto while Kazakhstan’s Rybakina was her own enemy for much of the evening.

Rybakina, the world number two, was broken twice in an opening set that also saw Swiatek save two break points to take ⁠command of the match. The first set was marred by 12 unforced errors ⁠for 27-year-old Rybakina, who struggled to strike the ball cleanly.

The Australian Open champion could not weaponise her serve either, with just one ace in the match, and Swiatek broke her again in the second set to take a 3-2 lead.

Swiatek, 25, dropped ⁠the next game but closed out the final three with confidence, landing a clean strike on match point to end her title drought.

“If she plays her ⁠best game she’s probably better than everyone,” Swiatek told reporters ⁠of Rybakina after the match. “You need to use all the opportunities; you can’t let yourself make mistakes or bad decisions.”

Fatigue had finally caught up with Rybakina, who played three hours more than Swiatek at the tournament before their meeting on Thursday as her ‌previous three matches went to three sets.

“I was just very tired. You could see that I wasn’t pushing with the legs enough,” Rybakina told reporters after the match. “There was a lot of unforced errors, especially ‌on ‌top of the net. It was just a pure lack of concentration.”

With the Canadian title, world number eight Swiatek will return to the top five in the rankings.

articles.title: Daly Cherry-Evans: NRL legend opens up on Hull FC move: 'It's where the connections felt right'
articles.summary: NRL legend Daly Cherry-Evans will swap Sydney for Hull in 2027 after signing a one-year deal with Hull FC; He will turn 38 as he joins the Super League club; he says it is a move to 'protect his future'
articles.body:
Cherry-Evans sensationally moved to Sydney Roosters ahead of the 2026 season and scored a try on Thursday in their match against Penrith Panthers to move his side top of the NRL table.

However, as he turns 38 years of age, Cherry-Evans will swap Sydney for the Black and Whites.

Former Kangaroos half-back Cherry-Evans is widely considered one of the best playmakers in the history of the sport, playing nine years for Australia and captaining Queensland.

While Cherry-Evans admitted he pondered about continuing to live the NRL "dream", his curiosity about Super League won out in a moment that felt like the "right time" to move across the world.

"That's just where the relationships and the connections felt right. I didn't have to look at too many other places, to be honest. If you're going to do it, you might as well do it properly, and Hull will give us that opportunity," Cherry-Evans said.

"As a person, deep down, I've always had that curiosity about what Super League would be like or what another code would be like in another country. As I've gotten older, I've understood that there's a big wide world out there, so it has become an interest, but I never knew when.

"I never had a timeline. It was just a thought that kept popping over again and again. It felt like coming to the Roosters wasn't just going to benefit me with footy, but also challenge me in other ways, and that's definitely been the case. It'll be another case of that in a different country next year.

"It just feels like the right time. No one can know when someone's right time is. It comes from deep within. The conversations I've had with myself and the people I love and trust - everything just makes sense to make the move now.

"There was definitely that voice in my head that said 'Stay in the NRL. Keep living out that dream.' But there's more to my story than me just playing in the NRL.

"I guess why I play in the NRL has a lot to do with challenging myself at the highest level but also inspiring my family and I feel like our family is ready for something different.

"We've had an amazing experience that's still continuing at the Roosters, but what an amazing opportunity I'm going to have to go and play in the UK with my wife and kids who will be old enough to remember it years down the track."

While all eyes are currently trained on Cherry-Evans' spectacular move, his are solely focused on ensuring that Sydney Roosters win the competition in 2026.

The move, in itself, was more about "protecting" the playmakers' future.

"There's absolutely nothing more important to me right now than winning a Premiership this year, but at some stage you do have to protect your future, and talking to my wife and the people we love and trust within our circle, we were told you will never regret going over to the UK and giving the Super League a go.

"We're really excited about what's ahead for us as a family and also I'm very excited about the challenges that the Super League is going to give to me.

"I am always about challenges and testing myself and Super League is going to give me that opportunity.

"But now that it's all done, it's great and I'm excited about it, but I can just drop the shoulders and just focus on everything inside these four walls for the rest of the year."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: New Zealand Darts Masters: Jonny Clayton thrashes Gerwyn Price in all-Welsh final in Auckland
articles.summary: Jonny Clayton claims second World Series of Darts title with commanding victory over compatriot Gerwyn Price in New Zealand Darts Masters final in Auckland; watch the World Grand Prix live from September 28 on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The Welshman defeated Gian van Veen and James Wade on his route to the final where he sealed his second World Series of Darts title with a 124-checkout finish on the bullseye.

Clayton hit a 158-finish to assume a 3-0 lead and never relinquished the advantage, racing into a 7-1 lead before holding off a late, three-leg rally to avenge his defeat to Price in the 2022 final in Hamilton.

"It was great to play in the final with my World Cup partner," Clayton reflected.

"It just shows that two rugby boys can play darts, and to play against each other in the world of rugby here in New Zealand, I've got a smile on my face.

"I really enjoyed that. It's 1-1 now, so next year - winner takes all!

"I'm looking forward to Wollongong next week. Hopefully the sun will shine on me and I can lift another trophy!"
